literal: The family of him who envies that which is given will perish, without even clothing and food.
translation: The family of one who envies the gifts given to others will perish, stripped of even basic clothing and food.
modern: பிறருக்குக் கொடுப்பதைக் கண்டு பொறாமைப்படுபவனுடைய சுற்றத்தார், உடுத்துவதற்கும் உண்பதற்கும் கூட இல்லாமல் அழிந்து போவார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet warns against the devastating consequences of harboring envy (அழுக்காறு) towards the charity or gifts given to others. The poet states that if a person feels jealous when someone gives a gift to another, it is not just that individual who suffers, but their entire family (சுற்றம்) that will face ruin. The ruin is so absolute that they will lack even the barest necessities of life: clothing (உடுப்பதூஉம்) and food (உண்பதூஉம்). The poetic lengthening (அளபெடை) in these two words emphasizes the extreme deprivation of these basic needs.
